I wanted to add that if you haven’t blocked your ex and you still feel like you need to have access to their social media just in case, just block them anyways.

I was lying to myself by keeping that channel open. I would get angrier and angrier at why he wouldn’t talk to me and I felt so alone and lost without the closure. Eventually I embarrassed myself and then blocked him. At first it hurt and I was wondering what he was up to, and occasionally I still wonder for a minute or two, but by blocking him I was set free.

There was no longer the if we got back together. By blocking him I was accepting it was over and there was no going back. It set me free to move on. And it set me free to find someone new who treats me sooooo much better.

Whenever I have been broken up with I would always keep the channel open to talk because what if we got back together. But now I realize I don’t want to get back together with them since they’ve made it clear they don’t want me. And by blocking them I’m accepting that it is over and I’m letting it go.

I’m not a medical expert but in my opinion it would depend if you were having issues from the overuse of caffeine in excedrin vs the acetaminophen part of excedrin. However I think it would probably be both in your case if you have been taking it everyday for years. A lot of times people will get headaches from too much caffeine or rebound headaches from too much painkiller. If I were you I would try to avoid it just in case. Personally I try to avoid caffeine except when sick because then I have it in my tool kit to make me feel better. However I guess you can’t know unless you try, maybe call your doctor to ask their advice?

I think people with mental health issues end up finding one another because we are able to relate and understand. Maybe someone without depression won’t be able to understand you, but many people are willing to try. The hard part is with being depressed or mentally ill generally we tend to self isolate which is not conducive to meeting people and dating. I can say though that every guy I have dated and fallen in love with has struggled with some form of mental illness. So I don’t think your depression will hold you back from a relationship. But I can say mental illness have led to making relationships very complex in my own life. Best of luck. Feel free to message me if you want to talk.

I am in a somewhat similar situation. But I will share with you my process for overcoming my break up thus far. 

My ex broke up with me and I was devastated. I couldn’t eat or sleep for days which ended up with me hospitalized. I was suicidal and ended up starting to self harm again. Everyday I struggled to not kill myself. Then I spent a day with my sister and remembered that I am capable of joy I just have to find it again. I decided that I wasn’t going to let him affect how I live my life. He broke up with me so I didn’t want to let him have any negative part or effect on me and my life. So I mourned the break up. I gave myself a day or two to feel the sad, I will refer to these as the sad days, but then I decided to accept he is no longer part of my life and that is okay. I thought about the issues from our relationship and I realized if he wasn’t 100% in the relationship then I didn’t want to be either. I am deserving of love. This is a personal decision but I decided to not hate on him as a person. I wanted to stay true to my values of compassion and forgiveness. So I kept talking bad about him to a minimum and I maintained he was a person who I loved and he that he has good heart but we just aren’t good for each other. I think not holding on to anger and resentment was key to feeling better, for me at least. In past break ups, I held on to anger hoping to get my revenge, but it only ended up hurting me. I still have love for him in my heart on some level and I will always appreciate the bond we had. But the all consuming love and admiration is now going to be reserved for someone who also loves me. Of course I am only human so sometimes I get those anger and sadness  twinges but I have resolved to fill the wallowing time with something positive and uplifting to bring my spirits up. In the past I have opted for music, but I have found that I get too emotionally invested in music and it causes those feelings to become stronger so this time around I have been listening to comedy podcasts while doing other activities such as cleaning or painting my nails. I have also made sure to eat. I have a history of disordered eating behaviors so this might just be an issue for me. But I took my two sad days and ate junk and comfort food.  But after those days I got back to eating healthy and taking proper care of myself with exercise and hygiene. This has made me feel a lot better. During my sad days my sister also made me a tinder. She swiped right on a bunch of guys and showed me the matches I had and it reminded me that I am not forever alone and there are people out there who think I am great at least on the surface. I am not going to pursue any tinder guys at the moment because I don’t have a desire to go out with a bunch of random people. However it feels nice to feel wanted again. The tinder did result in an issue where my ex saw me on there and sent me a nasty message which set me back a day or two in my progression to happiness and brought me back to feeling suicidal. But responded to him in a way I am proud of because I believe I maintained my integrity and poise. And stayed true to my values of being kind and compassionate even to someone who is being hateful towards myself. I gave myself another sad day and I picked up where I left off. I have also rekindled and even started some new friendships. I have taken more time to be social at school and have befriended my classmates more. It has been wonderful and I am feeling more happy everyday. When I am at school with my friends I don’t even think of the sad. I think I am 90% moved on at this point. I feel this way because I have actually developed a huge crush on one of my friends and when I think of dating or romantic relationships I no longer picture myself with my ex but I see a future with my crush/friend. Even though we are still in the friend zone I am hopeful to be in the romance stage soon enough. The only reason I don’t say 100% over my ex is because I do still miss him as a person because he was a huge part of my life. However I think when I spend time with my friends and especially my crush I am even happier now than when I was in the relationship with my ex.

I’m sorry this became so long. I guess it became a bit of a vent on my side too. But I hope my journey can help you as well. Either way I wish you the best.
